- HIL testing means the test of real ECUs in a realistic simulated environment. Usually a HIL
test system comprises the units under test, which can be one or more ECUs containing
new SW functions to be tested; real hardware components can be added to the test
system.
- While the ECUs are accessible by the use of tools such as INCA, the simulated
environment for HIL testing is created by ControlDesk platform.
- ControlDesk allows many features for the SW HIL testing:
✔ simulate driving cycles and maneuvers in specific driving conditions to check the ECUs behaviors as for expectations;
✔ monitoring the CAN frames for the real nodes in the loop;
✔ IO check in open loop test and IO fault injection.

in the model and the commands to simulate the vehicle drive (key position,
accelerator and brake pedal, gear shift, etc…). Many variables are added to show the
driving conditions (engine speed, PSA, drive ready, SOC, etc…).

- When adding the
model variables on the
plot editor, you can
measure the real time
behavior. You can do
that by clicking Start
Measuring on the
menu bar on the top.
- Sometimes, it could be
helpful to record the
model variables. You
can do that following
the procedure:
1. In Measurement
Configuration section create
a new recorder;
2. Select the variables to record
and drag them in the
recorder section;
3. Click on Start immediate to
start the record and click on
Stop recording to stop the
log;
4. The record will be available in
the section Project ->
Measurement data. You can
export it as .mf4 file.

- In case of simulated
nodes, you can override
the signals. You can
Generate a TX layout for
a specific message and
fill the values of the
signals, changing it from
input to constant.
- You can also:
✔ disable the message to simulate
a missing message, by
deselecting the Global Enable on
the top of the layout;
✔ change the CRC by deselecting it,
to simulate a fail on the CRC;
✔ change the message counter, to
simulate a fail on the MC.

- On the top bar, in the
section XIL API ESSPort,
you can configure and
add a new layout for
the FIU. Below the step
procedure:
1. Configure the ESSPort;
2. Select the pin
corresponding to the
sensor/actuator/CAN on
which you want to
simulate the fault. The list
is visible in the section
ESSPort Configurations
on the bottom and all the
available fault on the
specific pin are marked;
3. Drag the variable from
the list in the spot;
4. Choose and modify the
fault type (SCG, SCB, OL)
in the section Properties;
5. Download, activate and
trigger the event.
6. To heal the fault, click on
unload and deactivate

Signal generator
- On the top bar, in
the section Signal
Generator, you can
generate a specific
profile for a model
variable (for example
engine speed ramp,
cycling key off-key
on, etc..). Below the
step procedures:
1. Click on Insert Signal
Generator;
2. In Signal selector, choose
the type of signal that you
want to generate (segment
signal) an drag into the
bar the chosen segment;
3. Select the variable from
the model and drag it into
the spot;
4. Choose and modify the
duration/period of the
signal in the section
Properties;
5. Download and start the
Generator to trigger the
signal.

- Before starting using Control desk, check which project/experiment is activated in
the Project section. If you don’t know which is the correct .sdf to use, ask to your PL
or HIL team.
- Before starting using Control desk, it is recommended to reload the experiment; it is
mandatory to do it after an automation test.
- Before starting using Control desk, check that it is ONLINE and the Power Supply in
ON.
- If you override some paramenters or variables by Control Desk (for example override
the voltage on a sensor), then remember to come back to the nominal state after
your testing.
- If you change the value of some signals on Bus Navigator, then remember to come
back to the nominal state after your testing.
- If you apply some faults with FIU, then remember to heal the fault and to come back
to the nominal state after your testing.
- If you apply a stimolous with Signal generator, then remember to come back to the
nominal state after your testing.
- Before leaving the HIL, always key OFF, switch the Power Supply OFF and go
OFFLINE.
